```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Working directory

setwd("comp_bio/capture_c_adipocytes/main_screen/")

# modify accordingly

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, 
                      fig.width = 7,
                      cache.lazy = FALSE,
                      cache.path = ("cache/"),
                      fig.path = ("cache/"))

# Functions defined here
# copied from https://rdrr.io/bioc/imageHTS/man/zprime.html

zprime = function(a, b, method=c('mahalanobis', 'robust', 'fixsd', 'original')) {
    method = match.arg(method)
    
    if (method=='mahalanobis') {
        if (is.null(dim(a))) a = matrix(a, ncol=1)
        if (is.null(dim(b))) b = matrix(b, ncol=1)
        mua = apply(a, 2, mean)
        mub = apply(b, 2, mean)
        dm = try(mahalanobis(mua, mub, cov(a) + cov(b)))
        if (class(dm)=='try-error') NA
        else 1-3/sqrt(dm)
    }
    else {
        if (method=='robust') 1-3*(mad(a)+mad(b))/abs(median(a)-median(b))
        else if (method=='fixsd') 1-3*sqrt(var(a)+var(b))/abs(mean(a)-mean(b))
        else 1-3*(sd(a)+sd(b))/abs(mean(a)-mean(b))
    }
}


```

First things first, time to clean the data and assign the correct well and genes to each plate. The library of lentiviruses were rearranged by quadrant!
Using some excel magic, I've made a gene key and will merge them here:


```{r genekeys}

quad_gene_key <- fread("Quad rearrangements.txt")

quad_gene_key$Well <- str_replace_all(quad_gene_key$Well,"0(?=\\d)", "")

plate_file_names <- list.files(pattern = "SIMA_V1", full.names = F)

plates_list <- sapply(plate_file_names, fread, simplify = F, USE.NAMES = T)

all_plates <- rbindlist(plates_list, idcol = "plate") %>%  #figured it out... the order of plates is not 1,2,3 but 1,10 etc
    dplyr::select(-c("Number of Analyzed Fields", "Well URL"))

p1_3 <- left_join(all_plates[all_plates$plate %in% c("P1_SIMA_V1.txt", "P2_SIMA_V1.txt", "P3_SIMA_V1.txt")], quad_gene_key[,c(1,2)], by = c("WellName" = "Well")) %>% 
    dplyr::rename("Gene" = "Original")
p4_6 <- left_join(all_plates[all_plates$plate %in% c("P4_SIMA_V1.txt","P5_SIMA_V1.txt","P6_SIMA_V1.txt")], quad_gene_key[,c(1,3)], by = c("WellName" = "Well")) %>% 
    dplyr::rename("Gene" = "Stamp1")
p7_9 <- left_join(all_plates[all_plates$plate %in% c("P7_SIMA_V1.txt","P8_SIMA_V1.txt","P9_SIMA_V1.txt")], quad_gene_key[,c(1,4)], by = c("WellName" = "Well")) %>% 
    dplyr::rename("Gene" = "Stamp2")
p10_12 <- left_join(all_plates[all_plates$plate %in% c("P10_SIMA_V1.txt","P11_SIMA_V1.txt","P12_SIMA_V1.txt")], quad_gene_key[,c(1,5)], by = c("WellName" = "Well")) %>% 
    dplyr::rename("Gene" = "Stamp3")

final_plate_list <- bind_rows(p1_3, p4_6, p7_9, p10_12)



```

Z-scoring and effect sizes according to kevin's training:
Only with nuclei count so far, proof of concept

```{r kevinszscores}


which_plate <- unique(final_plate_list$plate)

all_plate_effect_sizes <- data.table()

for (j in seq_along(which_plate)) {
    
    # test
    #print(which_plate[j])
    
    temp_plate_list <- final_plate_list %>% dplyr::filter( plate == which_plate[j])
    
    
    # mean ntc for just one plate at a time
    mean_NTC <- mean(temp_plate_list$`Nuclei Selected - Number of Objects`[str_detect(temp_plate_list$Gene, "NTC")])
    
    # the sd
    stdev <- sd(temp_plate_list$`Nuclei Selected - Number of Objects`)
    
    # the effect size
    
    temp_plate_list <- temp_plate_list %>% 
        mutate(
            nuclei_count_z_score = ((`Nuclei Selected - Number of Objects`-mean_NTC)/stdev),
            sigma_z_score =  sd(nuclei_count_z_score[str_detect(Gene, "NTC")]),
            nuclei_count_effect_size = (nuclei_count_z_score/sigma_z_score)
        )
    
    all_plate_effect_sizes <- bind_rows(all_plate_effect_sizes, temp_plate_list)
    
}

### The non-looped version, which is also wrong bc it z scores the whole set of plates:
```

```{r loessforreal}
# OK OK. LOESS THEN Z SCORE

loess_dataset <- final_plate_list

variables_of_interest <- setdiff(colnames(final_plate_list), c("plate", "WellName", "Row", "Col", "Gene"))

rownames(loess_dataset) <- make.unique(loess_dataset$Gene)

loess_models <- lapply(variables_of_interest, function(x) {
    loess(as.formula(paste0("`",x,"`", " ~ Row + Col")),
          data = loess_dataset,
          span = 1,  # Adjust?
          degree = 1)    # Linear fit recommended for spatial patterns
})

names(loess_models) <- variables_of_interest

loess_fits <- lapply(variables_of_interest, function(y) {
    loess_models[[y]]["fitted"]
}) 
names(loess_fits) <- variables_of_interest


loess_results <- lapply(variables_of_interest, function(z){
    loess_models[[z]][["y"]]-(loess_fits[[z]][["fitted"]]-median(loess_fits[[z]][["fitted"]]))
})

names(loess_results) <- variables_of_interest

df_loess_results <- data.table(do.call(bind_cols, loess_results))

df_loess_results <- bind_cols(df_loess_results, loess_dataset %>% dplyr::select(c("plate", "Row", "Col", "WellName", "Gene")))


### Visualise the loessing if need:
# not fully corrected
# raw_map(data = final_plate_list$`Spots - Spot Area [px²] - Median per Well`,
#         well = final_plate_list$WellName,
#         plate = 96)
# 
# 
# raw_map(data = df_loess_results[df_loess_results$plate == "P1_SIMA_V1.txt"] %>% dplyr::select(`Spots - Spot Area [px²] - Median per Well`),
#         well = df_loess_results[df_loess_results$plate == "P1_SIMA_V1.txt"] %>% dplyr::select(WellName),
#         plate = 96)



### Z scores per plate on loess normalised data
variables_of_interest <- setdiff(colnames(df_loess_results), c("plate","WellName","Row","Col","Gene"))

which_plate <- unique(df_loess_results$plate)

all_plate_z_scores <- data.table()

for (j in seq_along(which_plate)) {
    
    # test
    #print(which_plate[j])
    
    ### SUBSET DATA TO PLATE LEVEL FOR Z-SCORE CALCULATIONS
    temp_plate_list <- df_loess_results %>% dplyr::filter( plate == which_plate[j])
    
    ### BEGIN 2ND LOOP FOR Z SCORE CALCS
    
    
    for (i in seq_along(variables_of_interest)) {
        
        #print(variables_of_interest[i])
        
        temp_var <- variables_of_interest[i]
        
        ### First get the mean and stdev which can change per iteration
        mean_NTC_var <- mean(temp_plate_list[[temp_var]]) # mean of variable across all genes
        stdev_var <- sd(temp_plate_list[[temp_var]]) # standard deviation for var across all genes
        
        
        ### Then get the Z-score
        temp_plate_list <- temp_plate_list %>%
            mutate(
                !!paste0(temp_var,"_z_score") := ( (.data[[temp_var]] - mean_NTC_var) / stdev_var)
            ) # this madness is needed for strings to become variable names
        ### Then the Sigma Z score
        assign(paste0("`",temp_var,"sigma_z_score","`"), sd(temp_plate_list[[paste0(temp_var,"_z_score")]][str_detect(temp_plate_list$Gene, "NTC")]))
        #print(eval(as.name(paste0("`",temp_var,"sigma_z_score","`")), envir= .GlobalEnv)) #debugging
        
        ### Then the effect sizes
        temp_plate_list <- temp_plate_list %>%
            mutate(
                !!paste0(temp_var,"effect_size") := .data[[paste0(temp_var,"_z_score")]] /eval(as.name(paste0("`",temp_var,"sigma_z_score","`")), envir= .GlobalEnv)
            )
        
    }
    
    ### ONCE ALL CALCULATED BIND ONTO PREVIOUS RESULTS
    all_plate_z_scores <- bind_rows(all_plate_z_scores, temp_plate_list)
    
}    



```

```{r zprimecheck}


### Z prime checks

z_scores_post_loess_only <- all_plate_z_scores %>% 
    dplyr::select(contains("z_score"), Gene)

a <- final_plate_list[final_plate_list$Gene == "IRS1"] %>% 
    dplyr::select(`Spots - Spot Area [px²] - Median per Well`)%>% 
    as_vector()

b <- final_plate_list[final_plate_list$Gene == "PTEN"] %>% 
    dplyr::select(`Spots - Spot Area [px²] - Median per Well`)%>% 
    as_vector()

c <- z_scores_post_loess_only[z_scores_post_loess_only$Gene == "IRS1"] %>% 
    dplyr::select(`Spots - Spot Area [px²] - Median per Well_z_score`)%>% 
    as_vector()

d <- z_scores_post_loess_only[z_scores_post_loess_only$Gene == "PTEN"] %>% 
    dplyr::select(`Spots - Spot Area [px²] - Median per Well_z_score`)%>% 
    as_vector()



zprime(a,b, method = "original")
zprime(c,d, method = "original")

zprime(a,b, method = "mahalanobis")
zprime(c,d, method = "mahalanobis") 

zprime(a,b, method = "robust")
zprime(c,d, method = "robust") # uses median, and is the only one which shows improvement

zprime(a,b, method = "fixsd")
zprime(c,d, method = "fixsd")





```


It appears that z factor + loess helped with the z prime score in only the robust one... Well I am just testing the spot area score


```{r top5genes}


### which genes are the most extreme then?

z_scores_post_loess_only <- all_plate_z_scores %>% 
    dplyr::select(contains("z_score"), Gene, plate)

which_col <- setdiff(colnames(z_scores_post_loess_only), c("Gene", "plate", "Row", "Col", "WellName"))
top_5_genes_zscore <- data.table(Rank = c("1st", "2nd", "3rd", "4th", "5th", "6th", "7th"))
temp_top_genes <- data.table()
for (i in seq_along(which_col)) {
    
    temp_top_genes <- z_scores_post_loess_only %>%
        group_by(Gene) %>% 
        summarise_at(vars(-c(plate)), median) %>% 
        slice_max(.data[[which_col[i]]], n = 7) %>% 
        dplyr::select(Gene) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(!!which_col[i] := Gene)
    
    top_5_genes_zscore <- bind_cols(top_5_genes_zscore, temp_top_genes)
}

top_5_genes_zscore
```
